title: Superior Auto-Identification of Trypanosome Parasites by Using a Hybrid Deep-Learning Model
protocol: Obtain at least 13 positive slides with blood-parasite infections confirmed by parasitologist experts.
Separate the slides for training (10 slides) and testing (three slides).
Acquire images of Giemsa stained-thin blood films under an oil-immersion field of a light microscope with a digital camera.
Obtain images containing multiple objects of trypomastigotes of T. brucei, T. cruzi, and T. evansi.
Look for slender shape, long tails, undulating membrane, and a kinetoplast at the anterior end in the images.
Consider creating both thick and thin smears to enhance detection of acute phase trypanosomiasis.
Recommend blood collection by finger-prick as suggested by WHO.
Utilize thin blood film images to maintain appropriate morphology of parasites for this study.
Store all images in a parasite-specific folder with 1,600 x 1,200 pixels and 24-bit depth as JPG files.
Split the images into training and test sets at a ~6:1 ratio.
Define the region of interest as a rectangular label for two classes: trypanosomes and non-trypanosomes.
Use the auto-cropping module to crop all detected images using the well-trained object detection model.
Collect a single object per image for training the object classification.
Open the CiRA CORE application from the computer desktop.
Create a new project by double-clicking on the program's icon.
Choose the required tools from the left vertical toolbar.
Select the training-DL model function for data labeling and training by using the drag-and-drop method.
Go to the General toolbar | CiRA AI.
Drag DeepTrain.
Drop DeepTrain on the screen (right-hand side).
Import the images using the DeepTrain tool's settings.
Click on the Load images button.
Navigate to the image directory.
Label the objects by holding the left-click and naming the selected object.
Adjust the rectangle line thickness and font size by clicking on the Display Setting button.
Save GT as a .gt file in the same directory.
Expand the data to gather sufficient information using the four augmentation techniques: Rotation, Contrast, Noise, and Blur.
Click the Gen Setting button to access this feature.
Initiate model training by clicking the Training button in the DeepTrain tool.
Select desired models, batch size, and subdivisions under Generate Training Files function.
Click the Generate button to create data and save it in the directory.
Choose options for Train function: use another generated training location, prebuilt weights, or override parameters.
Design model configuration and training conditions based on chosen options.
Begin the model training by clicking on the Train button.
Allow continuous execution of the program during training.
Evaluate training loss and adjust dataset weight during training process.
Save trained weight file in specified directory if optimal loss is achieved.
Select object detection model evaluation function for model evaluation.
Use drag-and-drop method to select EvalDetect from Plugin toolbar.
Drop EvalDetect on the screen (right-hand side) for evaluation.
Click on Setting.
Wait for Detection, Evaluate, and Plot functions to load.
Initiate model evaluation by importing the trained weight file via Load Config.
Under Detection, select non-maximum suppression (NMS) value.
Import test images from the image file directory using Browse.
Import the GT file from its saved directory using Load GT.
Choose an Intersection over Union (IoU) value for accuracy assessment.
Click Evaluation to assess the detection model in the specified directory.
The evaluation results will be automatically saved as a CSV file sorted by class name.
To plot Precision-Recall (PR) curve, import CSV files from the previous section via Browse.
Select classes from the list and click Plot to display the editable PR curve image.
Import the images from the image file directory by accessing the settings of the Image Slide tool.
Import the trained weight file (saved in step 2.2.8) by accessing the settings of the Deep Detect tool.
Click on the Config button | + button, select the backend (CUDA or CPU), provide a name, click OK, choose the weight file directory, and click Choose.
Within the Deep Detect tool, select the detection parameters (threshold and non-maxima suppression (nms)); drawing parameters; tracking parameters; and region of interest (ROI) parameters.
Select the directory where the cropped images will be saved by accessing the settings of the Deep Crop tool.
Click Browse | choose the directory to save the cropped images | click Choose | select the image format (jpg or png) | enable the Auto Save option.
Crop images to obtain a single object per image for image classification and segmentation.
Initiate the image cropping process by clicking on the Button Run tool.
Obtain a new image training dataset consisting of single-object images with a size of 608 x 608.
Use drag-and-drop to select the Image toolbar | DeepClassif | Drag ClassifTrain | Drop ClassifTrain on the screen.
Import images for model training using the ClassifTrain tool's settings.
Click on the Open folder button and navigate to the desired image directory.
Expand the data by clicking on the Augmentation button for more information using techniques such as Rotation, Contrast, Flipping (horizontal and/or vertical), Noise, and Blur.
Commence model training by clicking on the GenTrain button of the ClassifTrain tool.
Under the GenTrain function, select the models, batch size, and subdivisions.
Assign a directory to save the generated file.
Click the Generate button to proceed with data for training.
Tick the appropriate options in the Train function: Continue training with default weight or custom weight.
Initiate the model training by clicking the Start button.
Allow the program to execute continuously, evaluating the training loss and adjusting the dataset weights during the process.
Save the trained weight file to the specified directory by clicking the Export button when the desired level of loss is achieved.
Select the image classification model evaluation function using the drag-and-drop method from the Plugin toolbar | Evaluate.

Click on Setting within the EvaluateClassif tool to access additional functions such as Evaluate and PlotROC.
Initiate model evaluation by clicking the Evaluate button in the EvaluateClassif tool.
Import the test images from the image file directory by clicking Load folder image.
Import the trained weight file from the directory by clicking Load Config.
Evaluate the classification model by clicking the Start button.
Import the test images from the image file directory by clicking on the Setting option in the Image Slide tool.
Import the saved trained weight file from step 2.2.8 by clicking on the Setting option in the DeepDetect tool.
Click on the Config button, then the + button, select the backend (CUDA or CPU), provide a name, click OK, choose the weight file directory, and click Choose.
Under the DeepDetect tool, select the detection parameters (Threshold and nms), drawing parameters, tracking parameters, and ROI parameters.

Select the + button.

Click OK.

Check the predicted results for each image by clicking on the Run button on the ButtonRun tool.
